description: Two side-by-side engineering stress-strain plots, both with x-axis "Engineering strain (%)" from 0 to 90; y-axis "Engineering stress (MPa)" spanning 200-1200 MPa in (a) and 400-1600 MPa in (b), for Fe-Mn-Al-C steels. (a) shows the effect of Al and C contents: six curves labelled 22Mn-3Al-0.6C [72] (lowest plateau, between the 600 and 700 MPa gridlines, elongating furthest, past 80%), 22Mn-6Al-0.6C [72] (~690 MPa), the red curve 22Mn-0Al-0.6C [72] (plateau near 850 MPa, ending near 65%), 20Mn-10Al-1.0C [8], 20Mn-11Al-1.0C [8] and 20Mn-10Al-1.5C [8] (highest plateau, just above the 1000 MPa gridline, shortest elongation); annotation "Solutionizing 1000°C/1h WQ". (b) shows the effect of κ-carbide/B2 phase and heat treatment: 900°C/2min and 900°C/15min for 18Mn-10Al-0.9C-5Ni [22] give the highest stresses (~1550 and ~1380 MPa) at the smallest strains (~20-30%); 28Mn-12Al-1.0C [6] in 550°C/46min, 550°C/5min and WQ conditions gives progressively lower, flatter plateaus; the red 28Mn-10Al-1.0C,WQ [74] curve is the most ductile, reaching nearly the 90% gridline. No numeric data labels are printed on any curve.

observations.observation: Both panels plot engineering stress (MPa) versus engineering strain (%), with the strain axis running 0-90% and no numeric values printed on any curve (values must be read against gridlines).

In (a), the highest stress plateau is that of 20Mn-10Al-1.5C [8], lying just above the 1000 MPa gridline and terminating at the smallest strain of the panel, whereas the lowest plateau is 22Mn-3Al-0.6C [72] between the 600 and 700 MPa gridlines.
In (a) the 22Mn-3Al-0.6C [72] curve extends furthest along the strain axis, beyond the 80% gridline; the red 22Mn-0Al-0.6C [72] curve terminates near 65%.
Panel (a) carries the annotation "Solutionizing 1000°C/1h WQ" inside the plot area.

Panel (b) shows six curves labelled 900°C/2min [22] and 900°C/15min [22], 550°C/46min [6], 550°C/5min [6], WQ [6] and the red 28Mn-10Al-1.0C,WQ [74]; a separate legend text reads 18Mn-10Al-0.9C-5Ni [22] and 28Mn-12Al-1.0C [6].

The 900°C/2min and 900°C/15min curves of 18Mn-10Al-0.9C-5Ni [22] in (b) reach the highest stresses of the whole figure, around the 1550 and 1380 MPa gridline levels, but fracture at the smallest strains (~20% and ~30%).
The red curve 28Mn-10Al-1.0C,WQ [74] in (b) is the most ductile, extending almost to the 90% strain gridline at a plateau just below the 900 MPa gridline.

The labels "550°C/46min [6]" and "550°C/5min [6]" in (b) sit close together without leader lines, so the one-to-one assignment of each label to a specific black curve cannot be determined from the pixels alone.

The caption states that Fig. 22 gives typical engineering stress-strain curves of austenitic and austenite-based duplex steels, (a) showing the effect of Al and C contents and (b) the effect of κ-carbide and B2 intermetallic phase ('j0-carbide' in the OCR text), with heat-treatment details described in the text.

The citing text states that the 22Mn-(0,3,6)Al-0.6C steels of panel (a) were solution treated and water quenched with SFE in the range 20-50 mJ/m2, and that the Al-free steel has a higher strain hardening rate than the Al-alloyed steels.

The citing text states that the Fe-28Mn-10Al-1.0C steel (red curve in (b)) has the highest total elongation (~100%) of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steels reported, while Fe-28Mn-12Al-1.0C has a similar UTS, higher YS and lower TE (~65%).

The citing text states that the Fe-28Mn-12Al-1.0C [6] curves in (b) correspond to water-quenched and aged states (aging at 550°C for 5 min or 46 min after solution treatment at 1050°C for 25 min), and that the (a) steels were solution treated at 1000°C and water quenched with a single γ-phase microstructure.

The citing text states that the 18Mn-10Al-0.9C-5Ni steel (with 20% δ-ferrite, B2 stringers and nano-sized B2 particles) in (b) combines large ductility with a high strain-hardening capacity at yield strengths above 1 GPa.

The citing text states that increasing Al or C content and longer aging time raise YS and the YS/UTS ratio while decreasing total elongation, and that nearly horizontal stress-strain curves (even negative work-hardening rate) appear in highly alloyed Fe-20Mn-11Al-1.5C water-quenched (a) and in Fe-28Mn-12Al-1C after longer aging (b).

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves (y: 200-1200 MPa, x: 0-90%) illustrating the effect of Al and C contents on solution-treated (1000°C/1h, WQ) steels; six labelled curves, from highest plateau 20Mn-10Al-1.5C [8] down to 22Mn-3Al-0.6C [72], with the red 22Mn-0Al-0.6C [72] curve in the middle range. Longer plateaus correlate with lower flow stress.

Engineering stress-strain curves (y: 400-1600 MPa, x: 0-90%) for 18Mn-10Al-0.9C-5Ni [22] (900°C/2min, 900°C/15min), 28Mn-12Al-1.0C [6] (550°C/46min, 550°C/5min, WQ) and 28Mn-10Al-1.0C,WQ [74] (red). Higher strength accompanies shorter elongation; the red curve is the most ductile.
